key_insight: Training with multiple plausible fills for missing tests and privileged teacher feedback helps an Alzheimer's classification model represent uncertainty from incomplete data.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support more reliable model confidence when patients have different combinations of clinical, biospecimen and imaging data, but clinical utility remains unproven.
method: Generate several plausible completions, filling missing modalities one at a time.
Use a diagnosis-aware imputation teacher and a full-data diagnosis teacher during training.
Predict from a single generated completion at inference.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports outperforming state-of-the-art baselines on ADNI and competitive discrimination on two external cohorts, with calibration error matching the lowest after all methods were recalibrated.
watch_item: Training requires privileged diagnosis and full-modality information; prospective performance in routine clinical workflows is not established by the abstract.
paper_title: Privileged On-Policy Distillation for Calibrated Alzheimer's Diagnosis With Missing Modalities
